question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=- 4 x e^{- y}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =- 4 x e^{- y} \\ (e^{y})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =- 4 x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (e^{y})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (- 4 x)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (e^{y})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (- 4 x)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (e^{y})\,\text{d}y & =\int (- 4 x)\,\text{d}x \\ e^{y} & =- 2 x^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
e^{y}=- 2 x^{2}+C.
$$

generation.domain: all real x,y; right side plus C>0
